dataset.description: To ensure transparency, repeatability and consistent work with data, a research protocol and implementation guidelines will be prepared and made publicly available in Latvian. These documents will briefly and clearly define data collection methods (targeted and snowball sampling, semi-structured interviews, recording and transcription), ethical principles (informed consent, confidentiality, right to withdraw) and a reference to anonymity, as well as a description of thematic analysis with NVivo.

distribution.title: The project collects qualitative data to answer research questions and achieve objectives by mapping current practices, needs and barriers, as well as to inform evidence-based recommendations and implementation guidelines. Primary data will be obtained from semi-structured interviews with informed consent; participants will be recruited using purposive and snowball sampling; contextual secondary data will come from publicly available documents. Interview recordings/transcripts will remain confidential and will not be shared; only the research protocol and implementation guidelines will be published openly. All published materials will be in Latvian.

dmp.description:
The aim of the project is to investigate applicable legal frameworks and legal practice at international, regional, and national levels, determine the primary obstacles that offshore wind farm (OWF) projects would face, and develop preliminary legal recommendations for the introduction of more holistic OWF regulation from the OWF life cycle perspective in the legislative framework in Latvia. Firstly, the project examines the physical determinants of OWF development. Secondly, the investigation of applicable legal frameworks and legal practices to the OWF at international, regional and national levels is performed. Thirdly, in-depth semi structured interviews to identify challenges, conflicts, and difficulties of the OWF development and its legal framework in Latvia are conducted and analysed. The main outcomes of the project are the scientific papers and the study on the legal topicalities of the OFW development, which contains preliminary legislative proposals based on comparative legal studies and could be used in practice by state institutions and stakeholders. The subsequent applied research project application with an aim to prepare more elaborated rules concerning OWF regulation at the national level will be prepared.

Here, a description of the data collection will be given, which refers to the compilation of the bibliography and the preparation of the transcriptions of the interviews.

project.title: "Life-cycle of an offshore wind farm in the legal framework"
